01

The Authentic Name

Why ꜥanat.com is the correct form

Canaanite Original

Ἀνάθ

The name in its original Canaanite form. A name that carries the full phonetic weight of its source tradition.

ASCII Constraint

ANAT

Stripped of its identity, the name was reduced to plain Latin letters. The original orthography — stress, length, breathing — was erased by systems that only understand A-Z.

Unicode Restoration

ꜥAnat

The Unicode restoration recovers what ASCII destroyed. This is philological accuracy — not decoration. The domain encodes to Punycode, but the browser displays the truth.

Valid Scholarly Variations
Anat ʿAnat ꜥanat Anát

Each variant is an attested scholarly orthography. The owned form is the active domain; others are historically valid alternatives.

Punycode Encoding
ꜥanat.com → xn--anat-pe8o.com

The non-ASCII characters in ꜥAnat are encoded while the ASCII remains visible. To the DNS, it is Punycode. To humanity, it is ꜥAnat.

Tier Classification

Why ꜥAnat is classified as Tier-2 Basic

The Canaanite original Ἀνάθ contains only no distinctive phonetic features. This makes it a single-tier Tier-2 name. The Unicode restoration preserves what can be preserved — honoring the single feature that distinguishes it from plain ASCII.

04a

Unicode Registration Note

Why this flagship uses Egyptian Ain (ꜥ) instead of Semitic ʿayin

The historically accurate Semitic consonant at the start of ꜥAnat is ʿayin (ʿ), as attested in Hebrew ע, Phoenician 𐤏, and Arabic ع. However, the DNS root zone does not permit U+02BF (modifier letter reversed glottal stop) or the Arabic/Hebrew letter forms in domain labels. The only registrable Unicode workaround that preserves the phonetic identity of the consonant is Egyptian Ain (ꜥ, U+A725).

This substitution is purely a registry-level encoding constraint; it does not change the meaning, pronunciation, or Semitic sound structure of the name. The ideal form ʿAnat is still acknowledged in the Etymology section above.
